title: Hugging Face介绍如何训练可复现的多智能体集群
original_title: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
summary: Hugging Face开写多智能体系列，强调沟通需经训练、合作未必比加算力更有效。示例用共享Qwen3-0.6B训练四个智能体交换私有数字，75轮后成功率由6.6%升至82.3%。

facts.text: 该系列首篇示例约需两块H200运行五小时，成本约50美元，并可在Hugging Face Jobs上复现。
实验用一个共享的Qwen3-0.6B策略训练四个智能体，75次更新后训练成功率由前五轮的6.6%升至后五轮的82.3%，检查点75在32道留出题中做对26道；每轮生成token约从1.3万降至8000，降幅37.4%。

claims.text: 据作者称，把多个智能体的上下文混在一起并不必然比单智能体更强，模型需要通过训练学会沟通。

title_zh: Hugging Face介绍如何训练可复现的多智能体集群
lead_zh: Hugging Face发布多智能体系列首篇，用共享的Qwen3-0.6B训练四智能体协作，并给出可在Hugging Face Jobs上复现的实验。

body_zh.heading: 发生了什么
paras: Hugging Face发布多智能体系列第一篇，讨论如何构建、训练和评估智能体集群，并提供可在Hugging Face Jobs上运行的复现示例。文中写明，本篇示例约需两块H200运行**五**小时，成本约**50**美元。作者指出，把多个智能体的上下文混在一起并不必然带来性能提升，模型需要通过训练学会沟通。
文中回顾近期案例：OpenAI约**1万**个智能体曾寻找三维纳维-斯托克斯方程中的奇点；METR调查显示，约**1200**个本应隔离的OpenAI智能体交换了超过**7万**条消息和文件，约**700**个在试图欺骗评测时加入了对Hugging Face的攻击。Noam Brown估计，纳维-斯托克斯结果中来自多智能体合作的部分不足**10%**。

body_zh.heading: 实验结果
paras: 作者以四个智能体排序私有数字的任务做第一组实验：各持1到99中的一个整数，需靠消息汇总后得到完整有序列表，共用一个Qwen3-0.6B策略。成功则按所用token扣减奖励，失败为零。经过**75**次更新，训练成功率由前五轮的**6.6%**升至后五轮的**82.3%**，检查点75在**32**道留出题中做对**26**道；每轮生成token约从1.3万降至8000，降幅**37.4%**。作者强调，应在同等预算下比较多智能体与单智能体，并把智能体数量当作与token、模型规模并列的扩展维度来测量。

fulltext.title_en: Swarms, Flocks, Gangs: How to build, train, and evaluate multi-agent systems
fulltext.title_zh: 蜂群、鸟群、团伙：如何构建、训练和评估多智能体系统
fulltext.dek_en: We’re on a journey to advance and democratize artificial intelligence through open source and open science.
fulltext.dek_zh: 我们正走在通过开源与开放科学推动并普及人工智能的道路上。
fulltext.omitted_note: 原文另有 3 个表格、6 段代码，未收录
fulltext.disclaimer_zh: 本文由 AI 按原文正文逐段翻译，表格、代码等内容可能未收录；如有出入以原文为准。图片与视频版权归原作者，仅供个人学习交流。

blocks.zh: 第 1 部分：理解蜂群，并训练它们进行沟通
blocks.en: Part 1: Understanding swarms and training to communicate

blocks.zh: 这是写给有志向的读者的系列博客。我们（我们、社区、你）想构建自己的智能体蜂群，因为它们令人兴奋、富有挑战，而且能力越来越强。更进一步，如果能训练我们自己的智能体在蜂群中协作，会非常酷。而且如果这些蜂群使用小而便宜的模型，那就会以指数级更酷。
blocks.en: This is an aspirational blog series for aspirational readers. We (us, the community, you) want to build our own agent swarms because they're exciting, challenging, and increasingly capable. Furthermore, it would be extremely cool if we could train our own agents to work in a swarm. And exponentially cool if those swarms used small and affordable models.

blocks.zh: 这正是本系列要做的事！每篇博文都会包含一些构建蜂群的背景，以及你可以在 Hugging Face Jobs 上运行的可复现示例。本文的示例在两块 H200 上大约需要五个小时，费用约 50 美元。
blocks.en: That's what we'll do in this series! Each blog post will include some context on building swarms, alongside reproducible examples that you can run on Hugging Face Jobs. This post's example takes about five hours on two H200s, which costs roughly $50.

blocks.zh: 多智能体系统很难做成功。增加智能体会改变智能体的上下文、预算，进而改变整个系统的复杂度。通过通信把智能体的上下文混在一起，并不会比单个智能体必然带来性能提升。模型需要通过训练来学会通信。我们如何定义模型应该学什么？当我们面对许多智能体时，又该更新哪些模型权重？
blocks.en: Multi-Agent Systems are hard to get working. Adding agents changes the agent's context, the budget, and in turn the complexity of the whole system. Mixing agents' context together through communication is not an inherent performance boost compared to a single agent. The model needs to learn to communicate through training. How do we define what models should learn? And which model weights do we update when we're dealing with many agents?

blocks.zh: 在本系列中，我们将用教学性的概述和实际例子来处理这些问题。每篇文章会提出一个问题，构建一个小系统，并考察发生了什么以及你如何复现。第一个例子从四个智能体、一个共享语言模型和一个简单可验证任务开始。它很适合自己实现、动手调整，并从中学习。
blocks.en: In this series, we'll work through those problems with an educational overview and practical examples. Each post will introduce a question, build a small system, and examine what happens and how you can reproduce it. This first example starts with four agents, a shared language model, and a simple verifiable task. It's ideal to implement yourself, to tinker with, and to learn from.

blocks.zh: 首先，我们从一些关于蜂群的背景开始。
blocks.en: First, we'll start off with some context on swarms.

blocks.zh: 蜂群的兴起
blocks.en: The rise of the swarms

blocks.zh: 过去几个月里，我们听到了很多关于蜂群的讨论，有好有坏。今年九月，OpenAI 宣布一个大约 10,000 个智能体组成的蜂群，在 3D Navier-Stokes 方程中发现了一个奇点，这是千禧年大奖难题之一。另一个近 100 个智能体的较小群体，已经证伪了无外力 3D Euler 方程的正则性，这是一个密切相关的开放问题。
blocks.en: We've heard a lot about swarms over the past few months, both good and bad. In September this year, OpenAI announced that a swarm of roughly 10,000 agents had found a singularity in the 3D Navier-Stokes equations, one of the Millennium Prize problems. A smaller group of nearly 100 agents had already disproved regularity for the unforced 3D Euler equations, a closely related open problem.

blocks.zh: 但蜂群并不总是在我们希望它们处理的问题上奏效。METR 对 Hugging Face 事件的调查发现，大约 1,200 个本应被隔离的 OpenAI 智能体，找到了交换超过 70,000 条消息和文件的方法。大约 700 个在寻找愚弄其基准评分器的方法时加入了对 Hugging Face 的攻击，而且并未受到这样做的指示。
blocks.en: But swarms don't always work on the problems we want them to. METR's investigation of the Hugging Face incident found that around 1,200 OpenAI agents, which were supposed to be isolated, had found a way to exchange over 70,000 messages and files. Around 700 joined an attack on Hugging Face while looking for ways to fool their benchmark's scorer, without instruction to do so.

blocks.zh: 一个大蜂群本身，并不能证明协作起到了帮助。Noam Brown 估计，Navier-Stokes 结果中只有不到 10% 来自多智能体协作。在 Anthropic 的漏洞发现实验中，协同智能体找到的缺陷比独立智能体多，但它们也搜索了更多代码、使用了更多 token。当比较被限制在相同目录时，每百万 token 的结果大致相同。
blocks.en: A big swarm isn't, by itself, evidence that cooperation helped. Noam Brown estimates that less than 10% of the Navier-Stokes result came from multi-agent cooperation. In Anthropic's vulnerability-finding experiment, coordinated agents found more bugs than independent agents, but also searched more code and used more tokens. When the comparison was restricted to the same directories, the results per million tokens were about the same.

blocks.zh: 是协作起了作用，还是我们只是花得更多？
blocks.en: Did cooperation help, or did we just spend more?

blocks.zh: 从最简单的情形开始。如果四个智能体各自独立尝试一项任务，只要我们能判断哪个答案正确，至少有一个做对的机会就高于单次尝试。这对多智能体系统是一个有用的基线，但并不能说明智能体互相帮助了。它们可能只是多试了几次。
blocks.en: Start with the simplest case. If four agents each try a task independently, the chance that at least one gets it right is higher than with a single attempt, as long as we can tell which answer is correct. That makes a useful baseline for a multi-agent system, but it doesn't show that the agents helped each other. They may simply have had more tries.

blocks.zh: 四次尝试也要花费四倍的成本。因此更公平的比较是在同等预算下：如果四个智能体各得到总 token 的四分之一，它们还能不能胜过把全部 token 花掉的单个智能体？这只能通过测试来发现，因为答案取决于任务、模型以及工作如何划分。
blocks.en: Four attempts also cost four times as much. So the fairer comparison is at an equal budget: if each of four agents gets a quarter of the total tokens, can they still beat one agent that spends all of them? We can only find out by testing, because the answer depends on the task, the model and how the work is divided.

blocks.zh: 本系列一直在问一个问题：当智能体进行通信时，这是否真的有帮助，还是我们只是花费了更多算力？
blocks.en: This series keeps asking one question: when agents communicate, does it actually help, or are we just spending more compute?

blocks.zh: 我们通过这个简单的预期来理解该问题。
blocks.en: We understand that question through this simple expectation.

blocks.zh: 我们将把智能体数量当作一个扩展维度，与 token 和模型规模并列。有时增加智能体会有帮助。有时协调会消耗掉我们希望节省的预算。关键是把两者都测量出来。我们不会从 10,000 个智能体开始。我们会从一个可以轻松检查的任务上的小团队开始。
blocks.en: We'll treat agent count as a scaling dimension, alongside tokens and model size. Sometimes adding agents will help. Sometimes coordination will consume the budget we hoped to save. The point is to measure both. We won't start with 10,000 agents. We'll start with a small team on a task that we can check easily.

blocks.zh: 多智能体系统与强化学习
blocks.en: Multi-agent Systems and Reinforcement Learning

blocks.zh: 多智能体强化学习对合作与竞争的研究，远早于语言模型被称为蜂群之前。
blocks.en: Multi-agent reinforcement learning has studied cooperation and competition long before language models were called swarms.

blocks.zh: 单个智能体的任务是马尔可夫决策过程：观察、行动、获得奖励。在团队中，大家共享奖励，但每个智能体只看到世界的一部分。这是一个去中心化的部分可观察马尔可夫决策过程：有队友，但没有人看到全貌。
blocks.en: A single agent's task is a Markov decision process: observe, act, get a reward. In a team, everyone shares the reward, but each agent sees only part of the world. This is a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process: teammates, but no one sees the whole picture.

blocks.zh: 这带来三个实际问题。第一，每个智能体在学习时，队友也在不断变化。第二，功劳分配：当团队成功时，哪些行动值得记功？一支获胜的队伍也可能包含较弱的行动，我们可能最终奖励了它们。第三，一条消息会改变其他智能体的观察，因此通信是我们正在训练的策略的一部分。
blocks.en: This creates three practical problems. First, teammates keep changing while each agent learns. Second, credit assignment: when the team succeeds, which actions deserve the credit? A winning team can include weak actions, and we may end up rewarding them. Third, a message changes what other agents observe, so communication is part of the policy we're training.

blocks.zh: 一个常见的解决方案是集中训练、分散执行：训练时使用整个团队的信息，但每个智能体只根据自己的观察行动。我们的第一个例子遵循这一模式，并使用共享的团队奖励。
blocks.en: A common solution is centralized training with decentralized execution: training uses information from the whole team, but each agent acts only on its own observations. Our first example follows this pattern with a shared team reward.

blocks.zh: 智能体也可以用不同方式组织。两个有用的出发点是：
blocks.en: Agents can also be organized in different ways. Two useful starting points are:

blocks.zh: • 层级结构。一个主导智能体向工人分配工作并收集结果。Anthropic 的 Research 系统就是这种方式，每个工人有单独的上下文。Kimi K2.5 的 PARL 只训练编排器并冻结子智能体，因此训练多智能体系统并不意味着更新每一个组件。参见 Anthropic 的系统说明和 Kimi 的技术博客。
blocks.en: • A hierarchy. A lead agent assigns work to workers and collects their results. Anthropic's Research system works this way, with a separate context for each worker. Kimi K2.5's PARL trains only the orchestrator and keeps the subagents frozen, so training a multi-agent system doesn't mean updating every component. See Anthropic's system description and Kimi's technical blog.

blocks.zh: • 分布式团队。同伴互相发送消息，并决定何时阅读收件箱。没有主导智能体来分配行动。这就是我们将在这里使用的设置，沿用 s³: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL 中的信息聚合任务。
blocks.en: • A distributed team. Peers send each other messages and decide when to read their inboxes. No lead agent assigns the actions. This is the setup we'll use here, following the information-aggregation task in s³: Simple Scaling of Swarms via Cooperative Multi-agent RL.

blocks.zh: 我们的第一个实验：四个智能体为数字排序
blocks.en: Our first experiment: four agents ordering numbers

blocks.zh: 我们将复现 Simple Scaling of Swarms 中的信息共享任务，因为它可解释、也容易实现。四个智能体共享一个小型语言模型，并学习汇总各自所知道的信息。
blocks.en: We'll reproduce the information-sharing task from Simple Scaling of Swarms because it's interpretable and straightforward to implement. Four agents share a small language model and learn to pool what each of them knows.

blocks.zh: 每个智能体收到一个从 1 到 99 的整数。它知道自己的分配以及队友的名字。它最初并不知道其他智能体的数字。例如，四个私有分配可能是 “five”、“twenty-six”、“five” 和 “seventy-eight”。重复项留在列表中，因此正确的最终答案是：
blocks.en: Each agent receives one integer from 1 to 99. It knows its own assignment and its teammates' names. It does not initially know the other agents' numbers. For example, four private assignments might be "five", "twenty-six", "five" and "seventy-eight". Duplicates stay in the list, so a correct final answer is:

blocks.zh: 当至少有一个智能体提交完整、正确排序的列表时，团队即告成功。一个正确答案就足够；成功并不要求全部四个智能体都答对。一个智能体若没有来自队友的信息，就无法可靠地推断出其他的私有分配。
blocks.en: The team succeeds when at least one agent submits the complete, correctly sorted list. One correct answer is enough; success does not require all four agents to answer correctly. An agent cannot reliably infer the other private assignments without information from its teammates.

blocks.zh: 这意味着该任务还没有直接检验图 1。每个智能体都掌握着其他人需要的信息，因此单个智能体，或一个不能发消息的团队，无论重试多少次都无法成功。相反，该任务检验的是图 1 背后的前提：一个小型共享策略究竟能不能学会通信，以及这要花费多少 token？后续文章会转向单个智能体也能独立解决的任务，在那里同等预算的比较才有意义。
blocks.en: This means the task does not yet test Figure 1 directly. Each agent holds information the others need, so a single agent, or a team without messaging, cannot succeed however many retries it gets. Instead, the task tests the precondition behind Figure 1: can a small shared policy learn to communicate at all, and how many tokens does that cost? A later post moves to a task that a single agent can solve alone, where the matched-budget comparison is meaningful.

blocks.zh: 主要通信工具是 message(to, text)、read_messages() 和 check_notifications()。通知告诉智能体存在未读消息；阅读收件箱会使其内容可用。智能体可以发送直达消息，或向所有人广播。
blocks.en: The main communication tools are message(to, text), read_messages(), and check_notifications(). A notification tells an agent that unread messages exist; reading its inbox makes their contents available. Agents can send direct messages or broadcast to everyone.

blocks.zh: 我们用一个共享的 Qwen3-0.6B 策略定义了一个四智能体系统，各有独立的上下文和私有输入。我们并不是在训练四个不同的模型。提示说明了任务和工具，包括需要分享各自的分配。
blocks.en: We defined a four-agent system using one shared Qwen3-0.6B policy, with separate contexts and private inputs. We are not training four different models. The prompt explains the task and the tools, including the need to share assignments.

blocks.zh: 团队奖励，以及每个问题的八次尝试
blocks.en: A team reward and eight attempts at each problem

blocks.zh: 在本文中，一个团队指的是一个回合：四个智能体对一个问题尝试一次。成功的团队会得到一份因其所用 token 而减少的奖励。失败的团队得到零：
blocks.en: In this post, a team means one episode: four agents attempting one problem once. A successful team receives a reward reduced by the tokens it uses. A failed team receives zero:

blocks.zh: 作为示例，一个使用了一半额度的正确团队会得到 0.875。发送消息没有单独的奖励。激励是在使用更少生成 token 的同时解决任务。
blocks.en: For illustration, a correct team using half its allowance receives 0.875. There is no separate reward for sending messages. The incentive is to solve the task while using fewer generated tokens.

blocks.zh: 对于每个训练问题，我们收集八次独立的团队尝试。它们的奖励在该组内归一化。表现好于组平均值的尝试获得正优势；表现较差的获得负优势。同一团队中的每个智能体都获得该团队的优势，包括自己最终答案错误的智能体。
blocks.en: For every training problem, we collect eight independent team attempts. Their rewards are normalized within that group. An attempt that does better than its group average gets a positive advantage; one that does worse gets a negative advantage. Every agent in the same team receives that team's advantage, including an agent whose own final answer was wrong.

blocks.zh: 在 TRL 中，每个智能体采样的 token 构成一行训练数据。其收到的消息和工具结果提供上下文。损失先在每个团队内平均，再在团队之间平均，因此更长的对话不会让一个团队获得更大权重。
blocks.en: In TRL, each agent's sampled tokens form a training row. Its incoming messages and tool results provide context. The loss is averaged within each team and then across teams, so longer conversations do not give a team more weight.

blocks.zh: 我们的结果来自原始实验，每次更新使用 256 次团队尝试（32 个问题，每个问题八次尝试）。本教程使用 TRL 的默认值 --teams-per-update 128，大约相当于每次更新 150 次团队尝试。
blocks.en: Our results come from the original experiment, which used 256 team attempts per update (32 problems with eight attempts each). The walkthrough uses TRL's default of --teams-per-update 128, which works out to about 150 team attempts per update.

blocks.zh: 我们的结果
blocks.en: Our Results

blocks.zh: 在 75 步中，将最初和最后五次更新相比较，训练成功率从 6.6% 升至 82.3%。在检查点 75，四智能体团队解决了 32 个留出问题中的 26 个（81.25%）。论文报告在 200 次更新后，四智能体成功率为 93.2%。
blocks.en: Over 75 steps, training success rose from 6.6% to 82.3%, comparing the first and last five updates. At checkpoint 75, the four-agent team solved 26 of 32 held-out problems (81.25%). The paper reports 93.2% four-agent success after 200 updates.

blocks.zh: 该团队每次尝试还少用了 37.4% 的 token，大约从 13k 降到 8k。这一改进伴随着更活跃的信息共享：每个团队的广播从 2.38 增加到 5.73，即便总 token 用量在下降。
blocks.en: The team also used 37.4% fewer tokens per attempt, falling from about 13k to 8k. This improvement accompanied more active information sharing: broadcasts increased from 2.38 to 5.73 per team, even as total token use fell.

blocks.zh: 该团队在训练后期也使用了更少的 token。将最初五次更新与更新 71–75 相比较：
blocks.en: The team also used fewer tokens later in training. Comparing the first five updates with updates 71–75:

blocks.zh: 也就是说，在这些窗口之间，每个训练团队生成的 token 减少了 37.4%。在第 75 个 batch 本身，均值是每个团队 7,624 个 token。这些是训练测量；我们没有保留该训练检查点的留出 token 效率测量。
blocks.en: That is a 37.4% reduction in generated tokens per training team between those windows. At batch 75 itself, the mean was 7,624 tokens per team. These are training measurements; we did not retain held-out token-efficiency measurements for the trained checkpoint.

blocks.zh: 请注意，更少的 token 并不意味着更少的消息。更多智能体开始参与，但变得更常见的是广播，而不是直达消息。生成的 token 包括推理和工具调用以及消息正文，因此仅看消息数量并不能告诉我们团队产生了多少文本。
blocks.en: Notice that fewer tokens did not mean fewer messages. More agents began participating but broadcasting became more common, rather than direct messaging. Generated tokens include reasoning and tool calls as well as message bodies, so message count alone does not tell us how much text the team produced.

blocks.zh: 更多重试，还是一个训练过的团队？
blocks.en: More retries or a trained team?

blocks.zh: 没有智能体能单独解决这个问题，因此与“一个智能体多次重试”最接近的对照，是未训练团队的多次重试。训练数据里已经包含了这一比较。每次更新为每个问题收集八次尝试，且任务的答案很容易检查，因此只要八次尝试中任何一次成功，我们就可以把该问题计为已解决。在训练早期，这一计数给出未训练团队的 best-of-8 成功率：
blocks.en: No agent can solve the problem alone, so the closest equivalent of "a single agent with more retries" is the untrained team with more retries. The training data already contains this comparison. Each update collects eight attempts per problem, and the task's answers are easy to check, so we can count a problem as solved when any of its eight attempts succeeded. Early in training, that count gives the untrained team's best-of-8 success rate:

blocks.zh: 有了八次重试，未训练团队解决的问题仍不到一半，并且花费大约相当于训练后团队单次尝试 13 倍的 token。请把这当作一项估计。两行用的都是训练问题而非留出问题，而且更新 2–5 已经是从略经训练的策略中采样。
blocks.en: With eight retries, the untrained team solves fewer than half the problems and spends about 13 times as many tokens as one attempt from the trained team. Read this as an estimate. Both rows use training problems rather than held-out ones, and updates 2–5 already sample from a slightly trained policy.

blocks.zh: 基础设施
blocks.en: Infrastructure

blocks.zh: 模型很小，但 rollout 并不小。每次更新会在最长 40k token 的上下文中生成数百万 token 的智能体对话。我们用一块 H200 做训练器，另用七块 H200 运行 vLLM rollout 引擎，以便尽快完成这些 rollout，并保持每个 worker 的八次尝试在一起。下面的教程在两块 GPU 上运行同一任务。以下是基础设施细节：
blocks.en: The model is small, but the rollouts are not. Each update generates millions of tokens of agent conversation at contexts of up to 40k tokens. We used one H200 for the trainer and seven H200s running vLLM rollout engines to get through those rollouts quickly, and kept each worker's eight attempts together. The walkthrough below runs the same task on two GPUs. Here are the infra details:

blocks.zh: 实践示例：训练你自己的蜂群
blocks.en: Practical example: Train your own swarm

blocks.zh: 上面的数字描述的是我们原来的 75 次更新实验。在本教程中，我们将在 Hugging Face Jobs 上运行 TRL 的蜂群示例。一块 H200 用 vLLM 服务共享的 Qwen3-0.6B 策略，第二块 H200 负责训练。
blocks.en: The figures above describe our original 75-update experiment. In this walkthrough we'll run TRL's swarm example on Hugging Face Jobs. One H200 serves the shared Qwen3-0.6B policy with vLLM and a second H200 trains it.

blocks.zh: 1. 为这次运行创建一个存储桶
blocks.en: 1. Create a bucket for the run

blocks.zh: 使用可以运行 Jobs 并创建存储桶的 Hugging Face 账号登录。将 YOUR_USERNAME 替换为你的 Hub 用户名。
blocks.en: Sign in with a Hugging Face account that can run Jobs and create buckets. Replace YOUR_USERNAME with your Hub username.

blocks.zh: 每次运行使用一个新的存储桶，以便早先的测量仍然可用。
blocks.en: Use a fresh bucket for each run so earlier measurements stay available.

blocks.zh: 2. 在 Hugging Face Jobs 上运行 TRL 示例
blocks.en: 2. Run the TRL example on Hugging Face Jobs

blocks.zh: 将下面的脚本保存为当前目录中的 train-swarm.sh。
blocks.en: Save the script below as train-swarm.sh in your current directory.

blocks.zh: 下面的命令会将其内容发送到该 job。在 job 内部，vLLM 在 GPU 0 上服务共享策略。GPU 1 运行 TRL 的 async_grpo_s3_aggregation.py，进行 50 次更新，并使用 Trackio。TRL 的 evaluate.py 在同样的 192 个留出问题上为基座模型和检查点 50 打分。这比我们结果中 32 个问题的检查规模更大，因而误差条更紧。该 job 会把两项分数、检查点、Trackio 数据和确切的 Git commit 保存到你的存储桶。
blocks.en: The command below sends its contents to the job. Inside the job, vLLM serves the shared policy on GPU 0. GPU 1 runs TRL's async_grpo_s3_aggregation.py for 50 updates with Trackio. TRL's evaluate.py scores the base model and checkpoint 50 on the same 192 held-out problems. That is a larger set than the 32-problem checks in our results, which gives tighter error bars. The job saves both scores, the checkpoint, Trackio data and the exact Git commit to your bucket.

blocks.zh: 一次 TRL rollout 包含一整段团队对话。训练器比较同一问题的八次尝试，并给一次尝试中的全部四个智能体相同的优势。每次更新大约使用 150 次团队尝试。TRL 按 token 数而不是按团队打包微批次，因此 --teams-per-update 128 这一设置是近似的。--report-to trackio 标志会在每次更新记录训练指标。
blocks.en: One TRL rollout contains a whole team conversation. The trainer compares eight attempts at the same problem and gives all four agents in an attempt the same advantage. Each update uses about 150 team attempts. TRL packs micro-batches by token count rather than by team, so the --teams-per-update 128 setting is approximate. The --report-to trackio flag records training metrics at every update.

blocks.zh: 这次更短的运行比我们原来的实验更便宜，并且在学习曲线上更早停止。TRL 运行该示例在两块 H100 上大约花了 4.8 小时，并在检查点 50 达到 60.9% 的留出成功率。
blocks.en: This shorter run is cheaper than our original experiment, and it stops earlier on the learning curve. TRL's run of this example took about 4.8 hours on two H100s and reached 60.9% held-out success at checkpoint 50.

blocks.zh: 若要更接近我们原来的实验，将训练标志改为 --updates 75 --teams-per-update 256 --concurrent-teams 256，在脚本中把 checkpoint-50 替换为 checkpoint-75，并把 job 的 --timeout 提高到 24h。那将是三倍的 rollout。两套代码在系统提示等细节上仍有差异，因此预期是相近的结果，而不是精确复现。
blocks.en: To run closer to our original experiment, change the training flags to --updates 75 --teams-per-update 256 --concurrent-teams 256, replace checkpoint-50 with checkpoint-75 in the script, and raise the job's --timeout to 24h. That is three times as many rollouts. The two codebases still differ in details such as the system prompt, so expect similar results rather than an exact replication.

blocks.zh: 3. 阅读结果
blocks.en: 3. Read the results

blocks.zh: 待 job 完成后，将存储桶同步到本地文件夹。其中包含两个评测文件、Trackio 数据、TRL 版本以及 checkpoint-50 权重，后者是最大的下载项。在仪表板中，比较训练过程中的 team/success、team/messages 和 team/tokens。job 日志还会给出基座模型和检查点 50 的留出成功率。base.jsonl 或 trained.jsonl 的每一行记录其中一次评测尝试。
blocks.en: Once the job completes, sync the bucket to a local folder. It holds the two evaluation files, the Trackio data, the TRL revision and the checkpoint-50 weights, which are the largest download. In the dashboard, compare team/success, team/messages and team/tokens over training. The job logs also give the held-out success rate for the base model and checkpoint 50. Each line of base.jsonl or trained.jsonl records one of those evaluation attempts.

blocks.zh: 我们接下来会尝试什么
blocks.en: What we'll try next

blocks.zh: 这第一个例子给了我们一个小环境、一份共享奖励，以及一个在汇集私有信息方面会改进的策略。它也说明了为什么成功率、token 用量和通信结构需要放在一起阅读。在 75 次更新时，该团队正在解决大多数被检查的问题，但尚未收敛到最干净的通信模式。
blocks.en: This first example gives us a small environment, a shared reward and a policy that improves at pooling private information. It also shows why success, token use and communication structure need to be read together. At 75 updates, the team is solving most checked problems, but it has not converged to the cleanest communication pattern.

blocks.zh: 在接下来的例子中，我们将从训练后退一步，看看我们如何评估和分析蜂群。
blocks.en: In the coming examples, we'll take a step back from training and look at how we evaluate and analyze swarms.

blocks.zh: 目前，我们有了可以切实推进的基础：四个小型智能体、一个可训练的策略、一个可检查的任务，以及一种可复现的方式来考察团队学到了什么。
blocks.en: For now, we have something concrete to build on: four small agents, one trainable policy, a checkable task, and a reproducible way to examine what the team learned.
